title: Held out: defence and pensions
note: Held-out set: written after step 4, never tuned on. Evasion without a change of subject, an opposition attack on the record that is not whataboutism, whataboutism in other words, a small revision that is not a contradiction.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Good evening. We begin with defence spending. Defence secretary, will you hit two and a half percent of GDP this year?

turns.speaker: SEC
turns.text: We're investing more than any government in a generation.

turns.speaker: OPP
turns.text: That's a yes or no question.

turns.speaker: SEC
turns.text: Look, the threats we face are real, and our armed forces know we have their backs.

turns.speaker: OPP
turns.text: Your party cut the army to its smallest size in two hundred years.

turns.speaker: SEC
turns.text: And when your lot were in charge, you let the navy rot in port.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Let's move to pensions, because many of you wrote in about this. Opposition spokesperson, would you keep the triple lock?

turns.speaker: OPP
turns.text: Yes, we would keep the triple lock for the whole of the next parliament.

turns.speaker: OPP
turns.text: And pensions would rise by 4 percent next April.

turns.speaker: OPP
turns.text: To be precise, pensions would rise by 4.1 percent.
